# Cap-conditioned parity sources and exact joint-union capacities

Let C be compact and convex, S=C intersect (Z^n x R^d) nonempty, and
mu=H_q|S with q=dim_H S, positive finite total mass M. Let P be its
positive q-dimensional integer fibers. Let H_1,...,H_N be an ACTUAL
finite closed ambient cap cover of S. Write c_i=mu(H_i), and suppose
c_i<=B when a common budget is used. No below-OC cover is assumed to
exist; statements conditional on that budget are necessary data only.

This note constructs a finite dominated-source table using the entire
cap cover, with exact integer base means and a joint-union capacity
identity. It then records why these facts do not force a nontrivial
integer-tilt circulation after the proved <=2^n convex-partition
compression. The independent endpoint pair law is essential to the
explicit construction; no false mixed centroid-depth rule is invoked.

## 1. Symmetric pair law with the original source as BOTH marginals

For a represented parity r write mu_r for the original source on bases
congruent to r, and M_r=mu_r(S)>0. Define the finite pair measure

    pi=sum_r (mu_r tensor mu_r)/M_r.                 (1)

Its mass is M, it is invariant under swapping endpoints, and each
marginal is exactly mu. Every endpoint pair (a,b) in its support has
an integer-base midpoint y=(a+b)/2 in S.

This follows from convexity and parity, with the intrinsic alignment
proved in `candidate 93cf42ea22bcd767`.
The same construction works at q=0 with finite counting measures. In
positive dimension all lower-dimensional source fibers are null and
need not be added to (1).

For reference, if R_r(y)=H_q(S_r intersect (2y-S_r)), the midpoint
pushforward of (1) has density

    2^q sum_r R_r(y)/M_r                             (2)

with respect to mu, by the exact intrinsic correlation identity. In
particular its midpoint lies in P up to null sets. Formula (2) is not
a density domination by one and is not the differently normalized
correlation law with class weights proportional to M_r^2. The new
cap-conditioned source construction below uses (1), whose marginals
are the ORIGINAL mu.

## 2. A finite cap-conditioned integer-mean source table

Assign each endpoint pair measurably to an index i whose cap contains
its midpoint. The choice is symmetric in a,b. For example choose the
least such index. It is also possible, and useful in Section 3, to first
choose the least index containing BOTH endpoints when one exists, and
otherwise choose the least index containing the midpoint. A common cap
also contains the midpoint by convexity, so this rule remains valid.

Refine this assignment by the actual integer midpoint base j. Let
pi_(i,j) be its restricted pair measure, nu_(i,j) its first marginal,
and t_(i,j) its mass. Symmetry makes the second marginal the same. Then

    sum_(i,j) nu_(i,j)=mu,
    0<=nu_(i,j)<=mu,
    integral (z-j) dnu_(i,j)=0.                     (3)

The last identity follows pointwise after averaging endpoints, because
their base sum is 2j. For every positive entry, its full centroid

    y_(i,j)=(1/t_(i,j)) integral (z,x)dnu_(i,j)

equals the centroid of the corresponding midpoint measure. The latter
is supported in the convex set C intersect H_i at base j. Thus

    y_(i,j) in S intersect H_i.                     (4)

If L_i is any affine margin for H_i, the exact moment relation is

    t_(i,j)L_i(y_(i,j))
       =integral L_i((a+b)/2)dpi_(i,j)>=0.           (5)

In particular the source's integer-tilt contribution about j is zero;
this is (3), not a sign conclusion for a cross-centroid circulation.
If the cap cover is uniformly strict in these displayed margins,
max_i L_i>=epsilon on S, choose an attaining positive-margin cap at
each pair midpoint. Then the right side of (5) is >=epsilon t_(i,j).

These sources are generally fractional densities, not uniform measures
on convex subbodies. For q>=1 the proved simultaneous convex partition
theorem can realize their masses and BASE moments by actual convex
cells. That theorem does not preserve (4), (5), or their cap fractions:
continuous first moments and cap incidences are additional constraints.
No such preservation is assumed here.

## 3. Exact capacities retaining every actual union and overlap

Let T be ANY subset of the positive table labels (i,j), and let I be
the cap indices appearing in T. Define

    U_I=union_(i in I) H_i,
    pi_T=sum_((i,j) in T) pi_(i,j),
    nu_T=sum_((i,j) in T) nu_(i,j),
    t_T=pi_T(S x S),
    kappa_T=pi_T(U_I x U_I).

A pair assigned to a cap in I cannot have both endpoints outside U_I.
Indeed, if both endpoints were outside its assigned closed halfspace,
their midpoint would also be outside. Swap symmetry therefore gives
the EXACT identity and capacity inequality

    t_T+kappa_T=2nu_T(U_I)<=2mu(U_I).                (6)

To verify it directly, the pair types inside-inside, inside-outside,
outside-inside, and outside-outside have masses kappa_T, h, h, and zero.
Then t_T=kappa_T+2h and nu_T(U_I)=kappa_T+h.

Writing the actual source overlap correction as

    D_I=sum_(i in I)c_i-mu(U_I)>=0,

equation (6) retains it exactly:

    t_T+kappa_T+2D_I<=2sum_(i in I)c_i.              (7)

Thus the table has simultaneous finite-subset capacity constraints, not
just separate estimates t_(i,j)<=2B. In particular, for all table entries
with one cap index i, write their total mass t_i and double-capture mass
kappa_i. Then

    t_i+kappa_i<=2c_i<=2B.                          (8)

Under the common-endpoint priority rule in Section 2, some kappa_i is
strictly positive: a positive-mass cap in some parity has a positive
product-measure set of endpoint pairs both in it, and every such pair
is assigned to a common cap. Consequently if K cap indices have t_i>0,

    M+sum_i kappa_i<=2KB,
    K>M/(2B).                                      (9)

At a hypothetical budget B<gamma_d M/2^n, d>=1, this forces more than
2^n/(2gamma_d), hence more than 2^n, active CAP LABELS. It does not
force that many distinct midpoint bases: many cap labels may have the
same integer centroid base. This distinction is essential below.

The inequalities (6)--(9) are a rigorous budget-sensitive certificate.
They do not by themselves improve the ordinary total cap union bound:
the uncompressed cap cover can have many labels, and the geometric
quantities kappa_T concern the constructed pair law.

## 4. Sharp cube-simplex calibration: compression loses half-capture

Take S={0,1}^n x Delta_d with each simplex fiber of volume V. There is
the standard sharp cover by 2^n(d+1) ambient caps: at each binary base,
isolate its d+1 simplex centroid caps by a sufficiently large affine
integer tilt. Each has mass gamma_d V and its trace on every other
integer fiber is empty. Those caps cover every whole simplex fiber
because some barycentric coordinate is at least 1/(d+1).

Each parity class here contains just one base. Therefore every pair
in (1), every table entry in (3), and every assigned source stays on
that SAME base. There is no off-diagonal base transport or integer-tilt
charge at all. Nevertheless each base can support many positive cap
labels, so the cap-label conclusion in (9) gives no base circulation.

Any exhaustive integer-mean compression into at most 2^n positive
classes must have exactly one class per binary base, supported entirely
there. Each such source is the whole uniform simplex. Its centroid is
the usual simplex centroid, and an isolated canonical centroid cap
captures exactly gamma_d V of that class. For d>=2,

    gamma_d V < V/2.

Thus half-capture from (6) cannot survive this compression, already at
the actual SHARP OC budget. The lost amount in the quantity t-2nu(H)
is exactly (1-2gamma_d)V per base. For d=1 it is zero, as expected.
This disproves an unconditional half-capture-preserving compression,
not the conditional existence of a below-OC cover.

## 5. Rectangle calibration: the previously bad centroid caps are no cover

For S={-1,0,1,2}x[0,1], the minimum-base-variance partition has centroids
(0,3/10),(1,7/10). The centered dual caps

    x+z/5<=3/10,    x+z/5>=9/10

both have mass 9/10<M/4 but leave, for example, (0,1/2) uncovered.
They cannot be input to Section 2; the midpoint of pairs near (0,1/2)
is then not assigned to any cap. Thus the earlier centroid obstruction
does not contradict (3)--(9).

For comparison the following actual four-cap cover of this rectangle
has each cap mass 3/2:

    x+z/2<=1/2,     x-z/2>=1/2,
    x+z/2>=1,       x-z/2<=0.

The first two cover every point of the fibers at -1 and 0; the last
two cover the fibers at 1 and 2. It is a valid input for the pair table,
but its budget is above the OC threshold. No below-target counterexample
is claimed from either rectangle family.

## 6. Two precise obstacles to a circulation conclusion

First, the guaranteed parity agreement is between ENDPOINTS, not between
an endpoint and its integer midpoint. The pair of bases 0 and 2 has
midpoint 1. Requiring both endpoint-to-midpoint edges to preserve parity
would require a stronger congruence restriction, not the same 2^n-class
argument. Such a replacement is not made here.

Second, an exhaustive source-to-centroid flow with each destination's
true base mean has a variance drop. If p_(z,j)>=0 are its base masses,
sum_j p_(z,j)=w_z, sum_z p_(z,j)=t_j, and sum_z z p_(z,j)=t_j j, then

    sum_z w_z |z|^2-sum_j t_j |j|^2
       =sum_(z,j) p_(z,j)|z-j|^2.                   (10)

In particular if this finite flow is also a circulation with identical
source and target base marginals, the right side vanishes: all positive
flow has z=j. A nontrivial exact mean-preserving centroid transport cannot
be turned into such a closed circulation without a compensating marginal
term. Arbitrary integer cap tilts do not change this algebra.

The cross-centroid circulation from
`candidate 91db436274c254e2` is different: its
edge flow does not have destination conditional mean j, so its integer
tilt term need not vanish. The two uses of 'circulation' cannot be
identified. The new table and capacities retain actual low-cap-budget
information, but no definite sign for that different cross-centroid
charge follows from (3)--(10).

## Scope

The proved output is an explicit finite integer-mean dominated-source
table with cap-contained centroids, exact joint-union capacities, and
explicit compression/parity/marginal obstructions. The whole cover is
used throughout. No continuous gamma bound for arbitrary mixed pieces,
positive mass from outside every bad cap, or unproved source purification
preserving continuous moments is inserted. A below-OC sign mechanism
would still need a new inequality controlling the precise losses above.

`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_cap_conditioned_parity_source_capacities.py` checks every nonempty
label cut of an exact counted convex source, including boundary capture,
the integer-mean table, the variance defect, a source-to-midpoint parity
flip, and both rectangle and simplex calibrations. Its arithmetic is
exact; the general identities are proved above independently of the check.
